lines.text: Two diagonals cut a trapezoid into four triangles. We know just ONE area!
lines.caption: Two diagonals cut a trapezoid into four triangles. We know just ONE area!

lines.text: Top six, bottom ten, shaded triangle nine. What's the whole area?
lines.caption: Top six, bottom ten, shaded triangle nine. What's the whole area?

lines.text: Top and bottom are copies, sides six and ten: a three to five ratio.
lines.caption: Top and bottom are copies, sides six and ten: a three to five ratio.

lines.text: Areas grow by the ratio twice. Nine times five over three, times five over three, is twenty-five.
lines.caption: Areas grow by the ratio twice. Nine times five over three, times five over three, is twenty-five.

lines.text: The side triangles share the top one's height. Nine times five over three: fifteen each.
lines.caption: The side triangles share the top one's height. Nine times five over three: fifteen each.

lines.text: Now add: nine, twenty-five, fifteen, fifteen.
lines.caption: Now add: nine, twenty-five, fifteen, fifteen.

lines.text: Why are they copies? The full lesson shows two ways, plus every trap.
lines.caption: Why are they copies? The full lesson shows two ways, plus every trap.
